title: Unsafe Rust and FFI boundaries

spans.text: Goal: apply “Unsafe Rust and FFI boundaries” to a real program or device. The key principle is: The programmer must uphold the safety invariant for an unsafe operation. In a project, follow this guidance: Keep unsafe code in a small, separately reviewed API boundary.
QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.

unsafe permits operations such as raw-pointer dereferencing and some foreign calls that the compiler cannot verify. It does not make code safe: document invariants, minimize the block, and provide a safe wrapper.

permits operations the compiler cannot verify, such as raw-pointer dereferencing, union access, unsafe calls, and unsafe trait implementations. It does not turn checks off or make incorrect code safe; the author must define and uphold safety invariants. FFI must agree with the foreign library on ABI, types, buffer ownership, sizes, nullability, and destruction. Keep unsafe code small and add a safe wrapper, documented invariants, and tests.

What it does: The programmer must uphold the safety invariant for an unsafe operation.
Why it is used: Keep unsafe code in a small, separately reviewed API boundary.
If omitted or changed: Incorrect pointers, buffer lengths, or ABI assumptions at an FFI boundary can corrupt memory.
